description: APOAPSIS LAB is a team focused on science, space exploration, and technological innovation. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are developing APOAPSIS: Supervivencia Lunar, an interactive educational simulator that explores the challenges of sustaining a human research base near the lunar south pole. Our goal is to combine scientific concepts, engineering, and interactive technology to make lunar exploration more accessible and engaging.
summary: APOAPSIS: Lunar Survival is an educational simulator that challenges students to manage a research base near the Moon’s south pole. Players make daily decisions to balance energy, water, oxygen, food, temperature control, maintenance and scientific activities while responding to unexpected events. The simulator includes interactive mission controls, resource telemetry, engineering diagnostics, exploration objectives and a final mission report. A NASA LROC lunar south-pole illumination map is included as a visual reference to introduce real lunar environmental conditions. The simulation uses clearly identified illustrative parameters rather than claiming to reproduce NASA engineering specifications. APOAPSIS aims to make lunar exploration, systems engineering and resource management more accessible through interactive learning.
details:
How it works: Players manage a 30-day lunar mission, monitoring energy, water, oxygen, food, habitat temperature and an educational environmental index. They adjust power allocation, water recycling, heating, radiators, crew shifts, maintenance and scientific activities. They must respond to unexpected events, manage equipment problems and complete exploration objectives. At the end, the simulator generates a mission report and evaluates the outcome.

Benefits and expected impact: APOAPSIS introduces students to lunar exploration, resource management and systems engineering. It demonstrates how decisions in one subsystem can affect the entire base, encouraging critical thinking, problem-solving and scientific curiosity.

Creativity: The project transforms complex space exploration challenges into an interactive management experience. Instead of only reading about lunar missions, students experiment with decisions, observe their consequences and learn from different mission outcomes.

Factors considered: The design considers limited resources, crew habitability, energy availability, thermal conditions, maintenance, scientific priorities and the challenges of the lunar south-pole environment. NASA's LROC illumination map is included as a visual reference. It does not provide numerical input to the simulation; game parameters are illustrative educational values, not NASA engineering specifications.

Tools and technologies: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript and SVG. Development also involved AI-assisted coding, planning, documentation and review using Claude (Anthropic) and ChatGPT (OpenAI).
